-- The TARGET is these definitions, which also appear in the context: d15, S2, d3, d4, d16
def d15 : S1 Bool Bool where
  A1 := Unit
  a2 := inferInstance
  A3 := fun _ => Bool
  a4 := fun _ => false
  a5 := fun _ σ x => σ () || x
  a6 := fun σ => σ ()

structure S2 (X Y : Type) where
    B1 : Type
    B2 : Type
    b3 : B1
    b4 : B2
    b5 : B1 → B2 → X → B2
    b6 : B1 → B2 → X → B1
    a6 : B2 → Y

def d3 (P : S2 X Y) (xs : List X) : P.B1 × P.B2 :=
  xs.foldl (fun s x => (P.b6 s.1 s.2 x, P.b5 s.1 s.2 x)) (P.b3, P.b4)

def d4 (P : S2 X Y) (xs : List X) : Y := P.a6 (P.d3 xs).2

def S1.d16 {X Y P : Type} (N : S1 X Y) (v : P → N.D1 → N.D1)
    (xs : List (X × P)) : Y :=
  N.a6 (xs.foldl (fun σ xp => v xp.2 (N.d2 σ xp.1)) N.a4)

divergences.description: Relative to [P-O2] and [P-O3], S2 drops the requirement that weight changes be nontrivial (or actually affect activity/outputs) and abstracts away neural-network structure to arbitrary types B1 and B2. This widening is explicitly declared in claim (ii).

S2 restricts plasticity to deterministic discrete-time update rules b5 and b6 depending only on (B1, B2, X), so stochastic weight updates or external teaching/error signals are not directly represented unless encoded into X. In addition, the readout a6 : B2 → Y takes only B2 (activity) and not B1 (weights), so any weight-dependent readout must be computed inside b5 and carried in B2.

In S1.d16, interventions are deterministic, paired one-to-one in lockstep with sensory inputs in List (X × P), act strictly after each ordinary update (explicitly declared), and cannot occur on the empty list [] before any update; they also allow arbitrary state rewrites rather than physically constrained stimulation.

Relative to [P-U], S1.d16 only modifies the internal state N.D1 and cannot express structural perturbations that alter the network's units (A1), connectivity/update rule (a5), or readout (a6). However, claim (iii) itself only claims to model state-level interventions such as electrodes or TMS as in [P-D51b].

judgement.summary: The five definitions faithfully match the author's claims and the targeted aspects of [P-O2], [P-O3], and [P-D51b]: d15 is a one-unit latching system with indefinite input persistence, S2/d3/d4 define a general deterministic class encompassing discrete-time plastic systems, and S1.d16 renders state-level interventions as an input-output function over List (X × P). Only minor idealizations and scope caveats remain, notably deterministic lockstep dynamics, a readout not directly taking B1, and S1.d16's restriction to state rather than structural perturbations.
